Your hands do much more than help you carry out everyday activities. They may also offer important clues about your overall health. From unusual nail changes and persistent redness to swollen fingers and unexpected temperature changes, certain symptoms can sometimes indicate an underlying medical condition.


Although many hand-related changes are harmless, others may be associated with health problems such as arthritis, anaemia, liver disease, diabetes and even certain lung conditions.


According to Dr Donald Grant, a GP and senior clinical advisor at The Independent Pharmacy, recognising unusual changes in your hands can help you identify potential health concerns and seek medical advice sooner.


So, what should you look out for? Here are five changes in your hands that could signal an underlying health problem.


## 1. Changes in Your Nails Could Indicate an Underlying Condition


Your fingernails can reveal more about your health than you might expect. Changes in their colour, shape and texture can sometimes provide clues about infections, skin conditions and other medical problems.


One symptom to watch for is nail pitting, which appears as small dents or depressions across the nail surface. According to Dr Grant, this can be associated with psoriasis, a condition that affects the skin and can also involve the nails.


In more severe cases, nails may become brittle, crumble or separate from the nail bed.


Yellow nails are another change worth monitoring. While yellow discolouration is commonly linked to fungal nail infections, it can occasionally be associated with other underlying health conditions, including certain lung disorders.


However, nail discolouration does not automatically mean you have a serious illness. Nail injuries, infections and everyday environmental factors can also affect their appearance.


If you notice persistent changes in your nails, particularly if they are accompanied by pain, swelling or changes elsewhere in your body, arrange an appointment with your GP.


## 2. Red or Extremely Dry Palms May Be a Warning Sign


The appearance of the skin on your hands can change for several reasons, including weather conditions, allergies and underlying medical issues.


One condition to recognise is palmar erythema, which causes the palms to develop an unusual reddish appearance. Some people may also experience a warm or burning sensation.


Although palmar erythema can occur during pregnancy and may have relatively harmless causes, it can sometimes be associated with more serious conditions, including liver disease and certain types of lymphoma.


Another common concern is unusually dry or irritated skin.


Dry hands are often caused by frequent washing, exposure to cleaning products, cold weather or eczema. Allergic reactions can also trigger itching, redness and irritation.


In some circumstances, persistent skin changes may be associated with nutritional deficiencies or other health problems.


Using a suitable moisturiser can help manage ordinary dryness. However, if redness, itching or skin irritation continues despite treatment, seek advice from a healthcare professional.


Sudden or unexplained changes should not automatically be dismissed as a cosmetic issue.


## 3. Stiff or Painful Finger Joints Could Be Arthritis


Experiencing stiff fingers occasionally is not necessarily a cause for concern. However, persistent joint pain, swelling and reduced movement could indicate arthritis.


Osteoarthritis is one of the most common forms of arthritis. It develops when the protective cartilage within joints gradually breaks down, leading to discomfort and inflammation.


In the hands, osteoarthritis frequently affects the base of the thumb and the joints in the middle or at the ends of the fingers.


Common symptoms include:


- Pain when gripping objects or carrying out everyday activities.
- Stiffness, particularly after periods of inactivity.
- Swelling around affected joints.
- Reduced flexibility and difficulty moving the fingers.
- Small, firm lumps developing around finger joints.


The symptoms can gradually become more noticeable and may interfere with activities such as opening jars, writing or holding household objects.


Treatment depends on the severity of the condition and may include pain relief, anti-inflammatory medication, hand exercises and occupational therapy.


If you regularly experience painful or stiff finger joints, speak to your GP. Early assessment can help establish the cause and identify suitable ways to manage symptoms.


## 4. Unusually Cold or Hot Hands Could Point to Health Problems


Cold hands are particularly common during colder months, especially when temperatures drop. However, hands that remain unusually cold or experience unexplained temperature changes may deserve further investigation.


Persistent coldness can sometimes be associated with poor circulation or anaemia.


Anaemia occurs when the body does not have enough healthy red blood cells or haemoglobin to transport oxygen effectively. Depending on its cause and severity, it can lead to symptoms such as tiredness, weakness, breathlessness and cold extremities.


Diabetes can also affect circulation and nerves, potentially contributing to unusual sensations or temperature changes in the hands.


Another possible cause is Raynaud's phenomenon, a condition in which blood vessels temporarily narrow in response to cold temperatures or stress. This can cause fingers to turn white or blue before becoming red as circulation returns.


In some circumstances, a blood clot or another circulation-related problem may also cause changes affecting the hands.


If you notice persistent coldness, unusual colour changes, numbness or pain, arrange a medical assessment.


Seek urgent medical attention if a hand or finger suddenly becomes cold, pale or blue, particularly when accompanied by severe pain or numbness.


## 5. Swollen or Enlarged Fingers Could Signal Serious Illness


Changes in the shape or size of your fingers are another symptom worth paying attention to.


One condition associated with certain lung diseases is finger clubbing. This causes the fingertips to become enlarged and rounded, while the nails may curve more noticeably around the fingertips.


Finger clubbing can sometimes be associated with pulmonary fibrosis, a condition involving scarring of the lung tissue that makes breathing increasingly difficult.


It can also occur alongside other lung and heart conditions, so medical assessment is important.


Another symptom to recognise is dactylitis, sometimes described as sausage-shaped fingers because the entire finger becomes swollen.


Dactylitis can occur in conditions such as sickle cell disease and certain inflammatory forms of arthritis. Infections, including some bacterial infections, may also cause significant swelling.


These changes should not be ignored, particularly when they appear suddenly or are accompanied by pain, fever or other unusual symptoms.


If your fingers become noticeably enlarged or change shape without an obvious explanation, contact your GP promptly. Sudden painful swelling, especially with redness or fever, may require urgent assessment.


## When Should You See a Doctor About Changes in Your Hands?


Not every change in your hands indicates a serious health condition. Dry skin, occasional stiffness and cold fingers are often linked to everyday factors.


However, persistent, unexplained or rapidly developing symptoms should be investigated.


Pay particular attention to changes involving your nails, skin colour, joint movement, finger shape and temperature.


It is also important to consider whether you are experiencing other symptoms, such as unexplained weight loss, persistent tiredness, breathing difficulties, fever or unusual pain.


Keeping track of when symptoms began and whether they are getting worse can help your healthcare professional understand what is happening.


Most importantly, avoid diagnosing yourself based on a single symptom. Many different conditions can produce similar changes, and a medical examination or further tests may be needed to establish the cause.


## Final Thoughts


Your hands can sometimes provide valuable clues about your general health. Changes such as unusual nail discolouration, persistent red palms, stiff joints, unexplained temperature differences and swollen fingers may occasionally point towards an underlying medical condition.


Although these symptoms are not necessarily signs of serious illness, recognising unusual changes and seeking appropriate medical advice can help ensure that potential health problems are identified and treated.


Paying attention to your hands is a simple habit that could help you become more aware of changes in your body.

### Medical Disclaimer


This article is intended for general information and educational purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Changes in the appearance, temperature, or movement of your hands can have several possible causes, and the symptoms described do not necessarily indicate a serious medical condition. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional about persistent, unexplained. or concerning symptoms. Seek emergency medical assistance for sudden severe symptoms.
